## The finite-volume update and the flux divergence {#sec-ch04-divergence}

<!-- PROVENANCE

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- One stage forms $\Delta u = -\Delta t\,\nabla\!\cdot\!F$ on interior cells, then adds sources.
- The divergence is a difference of $AF$ over the two faces of each direction, divided by $V$.
- Switch: `dynamics/disable-flux-x1|x2|x3`, default false; disabling a direction also zeroes that gravity component.
- Flux form, so the operator conserves by construction on any grid.
- Geometric sources are added by the coordinate object, not by the divergence.
:::

Every scheme in this chapter feeds one operator. A Runge-Kutta stage reconstructs the primitive state to the
faces, solves a Riemann problem on each face to get a single flux there, and then books the net flux through the
cell. Written for one cell $i$ and one direction,

$$
\Delta u_i = -\Delta t\,\frac{A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2} - A_{i-1/2}F_{i-1/2}}{V_i},
$$ {#eq-ch04-divergence-fv}

summed over $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$. Nothing in @eq-ch04-divergence-fv depends on how $F$ was obtained: the
reconstructions of @sec-ch04-framework and the Riemann solvers of @sec-ch04-riemann only decide the number that
sits on the face. That separation is what makes the operator conservative whatever is plugged into it, and it is
why the two correction schemes of @sec-ch04-fluxcov and @sec-ch04-x1masscov can act on the face value alone.

### Derivation

The finite-volume balance over a cell is exact, not an approximation: integrating $\partial_t u +
\nabla\!\cdot\!F = 0$ over the cell and applying the divergence theorem gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\int_{V_i} u\,\mathrm{d}V
 = -\oint_{\partial V_i} F\cdot n\,\mathrm{d}A .
$$ {#eq-ch04-divergence-exact}

The only approximation in @eq-ch04-divergence-fv is that each face integral is replaced by one number times the
face area, so $F_{i\pm1/2}$ stands for the *face average* of the normal flux. Section 4B is entirely about the
difference between that face average and the value a solver returns from cell data.

Two properties follow directly, and `[C1]` and `[C4]` check them. First, on a Cartesian block the two face areas
of a direction are equal, so a flux that does not vary in that direction cancels exactly and a uniform state
keeps a bitwise zero tendency. Second, summing $V_i$ times @eq-ch04-divergence-fv over any set of cells leaves
only the fluxes through the outer boundary: interior faces appear twice with opposite signs. That telescoping is
the whole conservation argument, and it is why a seam between two processes must carry a *single* value
(@sec-ch04-seam) and why both terms of the 4B corrections are added to the face flux rather than to the cell
tendency.

On a curved grid the areas differ between the two faces of a direction and the cancellation is no longer
pointwise. What survives is the integral identity: `[C2]` reproduces $\nabla\!\cdot\!(r\hat r) = 3$ to
round-off from the code's own areas and volume, which is the identity the cubed-sphere volume test asserts cell
by cell. The remainder of the curvature, the part that is not a difference of face fluxes, is the geometric
source of @sec-ch04-sphsrc and @sec-ch04-gnomonic.

#| label: fig-ch04-divergence-stage

Each box is a step of the stage operator, in the order the code runs them; the colour marks which chapter owns the step, with orange the face work of this chapter, green the fourth-order face corrections of section 4B, vermillion the species limiter of @sec-ch08 and blue the implicit correction of the time-integration chapter. The divergence is the seventh box: every face value is final before it runs."

The stage is `forward` at [`hydro_forward.cpp:198-209`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L198-L209), which converts the conserved state to
primitive with `peos` and then runs the sweeps in the order of @fig-ch04-divergence-stage. The divergence itself
is `divergence` at [`coordinate.cpp:509-553`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L509-L553): it allocates one tendency tensor, adds the $AF$
difference of each defined direction over the interior index range, and divides by the cell volume. A direction
that is switched off simply has no flux tensor, so the same code covers one, two and three dimensions.

The index convention matters when reading the code. Cells run from the first interior index to the last, and the
faces of the same direction run one further, so the slices at `face_area1` ([`coordinate.cpp:534-538`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L534-L538)) read one more
face than there are cells. The tendency is written on interior cells only; ghost columns never receive one,
which is why a correction that writes a ghost column is harmless.

The base `forward` at [`coordinate.cpp:585-591`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L585-L591) is the Cartesian case: it discards the primitive
state and the face pressure and returns the divergence alone. Every curved coordinate overrides it and adds its
source on top of the same divergence.

| quantity | lives at | from |
|---|---|---|
| $F_1$, $F_2$, $F_3$ | faces of its own direction | the Riemann solver, then the species limiter |
| $A_{i\pm1/2}$, $V_i$ | faces, cells | `face_area1`, `cell_volume` |
| $\Delta u$ | interior cells | minus $\Delta t$ times the divergence |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Cylindrical coordinates are not built: the source file carries a trailing underscore and is not compiled.
- A uniform state is preserved bitwise only on a Cartesian block; on a curved grid the cancellation is an
  integral identity and holds to round-off, not bitwise.
:::

1. **Ghost tendencies.** No tendency is ever formed on a ghost cell, so a correction that writes one cannot
   reach the state. That is a property of the current index ranges, not something the code asserts.
2. **One value per face.** The operator assumes each face carries one number. Where two processes own the same
   face that has to be arranged explicitly (@sec-ch04-seam); where the two sides disagree, averaging hides the
   disagreement rather than removing it.
